decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY changing enable_gpio from GPIO3 to GPIO5.
The LEDs are powered by the switched 5V rail, whose 5V_EN control assignment necessarily changes from GPIO3 to GPIO5.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: That was my mistake: GPIO3 came from my original ESP32 design. Use GPIO5 for 5V_EN instead. I also realized that GPIO22, GPIO23, GPIO25, and GPIO27 are not exposed on the WROOM-1 module, so SCL0 must move from GPIO22 to GPIO38 and SPI MOSI from GPIO23 to GPIO26. I'll update the documentation and send you the complete revised GPIO table.

value_updates.power_switching: The LED-supplying 5V rail is controlled by ESP32 GPIO5

decisions.reason: The GPIO reassignment does not change the standalone USB-powered 3.3V rail, its activation condition, or its powered scope.
The GPIO reassignment does not alter the OR-ing topology, power sources, or source-selection behavior.
The charge-status indicator remains assigned to GPIO13 and is unaffected by the 5V_EN, SCL0, and SPI MOSI reassignments.
The source changes MCU GPIO assignments behind the named SCL0 and 5V_EN signals but does not change their interboard connector positions or signal names.
Moving SCL0 to GPIO38 does not change the I2C cable length, clock speed, pull-up configuration, or series-resistor policy.
The ESP32 GPIO changes do not affect the AXP2101 VMID/VSYS topology or net labeling.
The source does not change the LED board's count or addressable-LED requirement.
The GPIO reassignment does not affect the battery connector, placement, mounting style, or unresolved battery pinout.
The source does not alter battery overcharge, overdischarge, or thermal-protection behavior.
The battery NTC monitoring connection through J_BAT is unaffected by the ESP32 GPIO reassignments.
